items.item_text: Senior Human Resources Professional Certification (SHRM-SCP or SPHR).
OD certification, related certification, or completion of related formal training program (e.g., Organizational Design, Change Management, Assessment Tools, Coaching, etc.)
Bachelors degree in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Business Administration, Social Sciences, Public Administration, Healthcare Administration, or related field.
Masters degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, Public Administration, Social Sciences, Healthcare Administration, or related field.
Ten (10) years experience in human resources, business operations, or a related field.
Minimum eight (8) years experience in managing talent management processes (e.g. talent acquisition, performance evaluations, organizational development, succession planning, etc.).
Five (5) years of leadership experience with or without direct reports, including at least two (2) years of formal supervisory experience.
Five (5) years of experience requiring workforce analytics, reporting, and business analysis.
Five (5) years experience in managing talent management processes (e.g. talent acquisition, performance evaluations, organizational development, succession planning, etc.).
Five (5) years of experience in business analysis, including defining business requirements and validating solutions.
Two (2) years experience developing and implementing employee engagement and recognition programs or initiatives.
Four (4) years of experience managing operational or departmental budgets.
Two (2) years experience in organizational effectiveness (e.g. change management, organization design and structure, structured decision making, leadership coaching, etc.).
Three (3) years of project management and/or process improvement experience or related certification (e.g., PMP, Lean Six Sigma).
Experience developing and implementing workforce strategies and HR programs that support organizational objectives.
Five (5) years experience in the design and execution of people listening instruments (e.g. surveys, focus groups, interviews).
Demonstrated experience using workforce analytics, business metrics, and reporting to support strategic decision making.
Five (5) years of experience as an HR Generalist or supporting multiple HR disciplines.
Five (5) years experience working cross-functionally across departments, functions, or business lines.
Experience within academic medicine, higher education, or other complex matrixed organizations.
Develop and execute human resources, talent acquisition and management strategies that align with KPSOMs mission, strategic priorities, and workforce objectives.

Partner with executive and departmental leaders to assess workforce needs, identify organizational risks and opportunities, and develop solutions that strengthen organizational effectiveness, talent management and workforce capability.
Serve as a trusted advisor on workforce strategy, organizational design, talent acquisition and management, employee engagement, leadership effectiveness, and organizational change.

Direct talent management programs, including talent acquisition, workforce planning, succession planning, performance management, leadership development, employee development, recognition, and retention.
Lead organizational development and change management initiatives that enhance organizational capability, culture, employee engagement, and team effectiveness.
Oversee the design, delivery, and evaluation of learning and development programs aligned with workforce planning objectives, organizational culture, and business strategy.
Partner with HR Business Partners and organizational leaders to identify workforce, leadership, and capability gaps and implement targeted solutions to address current and future needs.
Direct the design, implementation, administration, and continuous improvement of HR programs, processes, systems, and tools to ensure efficient and effective service delivery.
Provide leadership for day-to-day HR operations, ensuring compliance, operational excellence, customer-focused service, and a positive employee experience.
Oversee workforce analytics, metrics, dashboards, and reporting to evaluate organizational health, measure HR program effectiveness, and support data-driven decision making.
Lead continuous improvement efforts to enhance HR operations, service quality, workforce outcomes, and organizational performance.
Direct organizational design, restructuring, integration, and workforce transition initiatives to ensure alignment with strategic and operational objectives.
Lead, develop, and mentor HR staff through effective recruitment, performance management, coaching, and professional development practices.
Represent Human Resources on institutional committees, cross-functional initiatives, and serve as a delegate for HR leadership as assigned.
Strong project management, organizational effectiveness, and change management capabilities.
Demonstrated knowledge of federal and state employment laws, HR regulations, and workforce compliance requirements.
Strong business acumen and ability to align workforce strategies with organizational goals.
Excellent communication, facilitation, consulting, and relationship management skills.
Ability to manage sensitive and confidential information while exercising sound judgment and discretion.
